note: Indonesian startups that stopped operating. Compiled and source-checked; nothing is listed without a date and at least one link. Empty is the correct state until entries pass verification.

entries.name: eFishery
entries.sector: Agritech — aquaculture feeders, feed distribution and farmer financing
entries.why: Indonesia's first aquaculture unicorn, valued at US$1.4bn on a US$200M Series D in July 2023 and reported to have raised about US$415M in all. A forensic audit opened in December 2024 found the accounts had been inflated — FTI Consulting's reading put the overstatement near US$600M — and the board suspended co-founder and CEO Gibran Huzaifah. New management cut roughly 90% of some 1,500 staff in February 2025, operations stopped, and a sale of the technology portfolio has since stalled. Huzaifah was sentenced to nine years in April 2026 for embezzlement and money laundering. Marked REPORTED, not confirmed: the company has published no shutdown notice and no completed liquidation is on record — the entity was expected to be wound up by the end of 2025 with its books closing around April 2026.

entries.name: Delegasi
entries.sector: SaaS — automated bookkeeping for small businesses
entries.why: Y Combinator S22, and the first virtual financial manager pitched at Indonesian F&B owners. Wound down around August 2025: co-founder and CTO Ahmad Anshorimuslim Syuhada's own profile says he “ultimately made the decision to wind down the company, preserving capital, team integrity, and long-term optionality”, and his post of 30 Sep 2025 dates it to about a month earlier. YC's directory marks the batch entry Inactive. delegasi.co and the LinkedIn page are both still up, which is why this row exists — the site being live is not the same as the company being live. US$125K, the YC standard deal, is the only figure ever disclosed; BEENEXT was reported in a 2022 seed round without one.

entries.name: Ritase
entries.why: One of Indonesia's first digital-trucking platforms (founded by Iman Kusnadi and David Samuel), matching shippers with transporters at tens of thousands of shipments a month. Raised a US$8.5M Series A led by Golden Gate Ventures with Jafco Asia and ZWC in Jul 2019, on top of US$4.4M of seed and pre-Series A money from Insignia Ventures, Mitsubishi Corporation, BEENEXT, Skystar Capital and Agung — about US$12.9M in all (KrASIA, citing the company). Through 2023 Tech in Asia reported distress-sale talks after mass layoffs, and on 24 Nov 2023 DealStreetAsia reported that Meratus, the Surabaya maritime logistics group, had bought its technology assets. ritase.com no longer resolves (HTTP 404 on apex and www, checked 30 Aug 2026). Marked REPORTED: the company itself published no closure notice, and the asset sale is sourced to DealStreetAsia's reporting.
